name: Source-Spectral Zero Criterion and Gap
statement: For a nonempty union-closed class, let $k(C)$ be the largest number of present right-side terms in a positive source row, with minimum convention one. Then $d_{\mathrm{sp}}(C)=0$ exactly when some shared array has $\beta_C/\alpha_C<1/k(C)$, and exactly when the class has a strict term-dominance certificate. Hence $d_{\mathrm{sp}}=0$ or $d_{\mathrm{sp}}\ge1/k(C)$. For a class on $n$ coordinates admitting a union-closed orientation, $\delta_{\mathrm{sp}}=0$ exactly when strict term dominance holds, and every nonzero value is at least $1/\max(1,n-1)$.
proof: A spectral ratio below $1/k$ permits a common scale at which positive sums divided by $k$ and negative sums are feasible; a largest positive term then dominates. Conversely, raise every coefficient and witness magnitude in a strict dominance certificate to a common power. Favorable maxima grow by $A^t$ while each unfavorable sum is at most a fixed row-size factor times $B^t$, with $A>1>B>0$, driving $\beta/\alpha$ to zero.
